title: JANUS Storm / Control-Plane Investigation Journal

included: public provider statements and technical documentation
public witness reports and public repositories when directly relevant
JANUS Record Drift Observatory scheduler measurements as reference evidence
user-preserved JANUS artifacts relevant to timing, causality, cancellation, rollback and observer discipline
hypotheses with explicit evidence grades, falsifiers and negative controls
excluded: local engineering diagnostics not required to reproduce the external investigation

epistemic_constitution.rule: SIGNAL != CAUSE; CAUSE != INTENT; INTENT != IDENTITY; IDENTITY != GUILT.
epistemic_constitution.claim_ceiling: Temporal overlap, technical similarity, or a plausible mechanism must not be promoted into shared-cause or attacker attribution without an independent bridge.
method_requirements: distinguish correlation, cause, intentional cause and identity

github_reference_measurements.interpretation: The measured delay is concentrated before GitHub run-object materialization rather than after runner allocation.

semantic_boundary: The seven delayed events are Genesis narrative/event semantics in which consequences of earlier actions surface later; they are not network or scheduler latency evidence.
EXIT_CANCELLED is an in-world Genesis state transition, not ChatGPT transport cancellation evidence.

riders_of_the_storm.boundary: Riders of Justice artifacts were found and are methodologically relevant but must not be renamed or substituted for Riders of the Storm.

reported_observation: A ChatGPT-mediated operation was arranged to act at a specified time and post/send three files.
During an observed delay window the user issued a cancellation instruction.
The user reports that the files/data nevertheless completed the outbound side effect.
The user regarded this as a vulnerability/race condition and wanted a controlled follow-up experiment.
not_yet_proven: whether cancellation reached the same subsystem that owned the side effect
whether cancellation acknowledgment occurred before or after an irreversible commit boundary
whether the three file operations shared one transaction or independent queues
promotion_gate: recover original conversation/tool receipt or export
recover cancellation request and acknowledgement timestamps
recover a receipt for each file side effect
prefer monotonic ordering over display timestamps alone
user_reported_july_chatgpt_timing_case.security_boundary: Do not probe production systems as an exploit. Any future authorized reproduction must use harmless test data and an explicitly permitted sandbox.

rules: old signatures prove authenticity but not freshness
an external freshness root is required outside the rollback domain
coordinate timestamps are not anti-rollback evidence
separate information dependence from ordering/provenance effects
include shared memory/cache/network side channels and latent common causes
freeze the causal DAG before decisive runs
backdated coordinate timestamps do not override monotonic execution order
post-selection is rejected as future-information evidence
self-consistent copy loops are not independent future information
freeze queue topology, monotonic clock identity/resolution and instrumentation schema
measure checkpoint visibility latency, queue depth and control-plane response latency
do not recalibrate after seeing the outcome

tspu_branch.hypothesis: Selective or staged TSPU/DPI rule deployment can produce partial, protocol-specific, route-specific and temporally staggered failures rather than a single all-network outage.

evidence.finding: TSPU are DPI complexes that can block or slow traffic using IP, SNI, QUIC metadata, protocol signatures and other criteria; effects can be intermittent and can affect cross-border traffic.

The report observed UDP DNS queries nominally sent to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 returning NXDOMAIN for tested blocked domains while TCP DNS returned real answers; TTL/ICMP observations were interpreted as destination rewriting toward 195.208.5.1.
evidence.claim_ceiling: Strong public technical evidence of contemporaneous selective DNS interference, not an official admission and not evidence that GitHub's internal scheduler incident was caused by TSPU.

evidence.finding: Telegram anomalies appeared across many Russian ASes with resets/timeouts but were not visible on all tested networks, demonstrating heterogeneous/selective effects.
Providers reported TSPU deployment at exits of some Russian data-center nodes and described recent tests affecting GitHub, App Store and other application-store traffic.
Daily ISP/server/strategy measurements show route- and destination-specific blocking states.
Community participants reported Telegram/TSPU rule effects appearing first east of the Urals and later reaching Moscow, consistent with a staged rollout pattern.
evidence.claim_ceiling: Community observation, not an official rollout log.

evidence.finding: Pavel Durov attributed a payment-system disruption to VPN blocking; Sberbank acknowledged a technical issue but did not publicly establish that causal explanation.

new_fact.statement: A selective Russian-network DNS interference change was publicly measured beginning approximately the evening of Aug 26, overlapping the wider investigation period.

hypothesis_matrix.hypothesis: GitHub Aug 26 Actions failure was driven by GitHub-internal trigger/event-processing overload and database write saturation.
Residual schedule registration/materialization failures persisted beyond the broad GitHub resolved window for some repositories.
TSPU/selective filtering can cause partial and temporally staggered failures inside or across Russian networks.
The Aug 26-27 TSPU changes caused GitHub's global/internal Actions scheduler incident.
Russian authorities were deliberately probing capabilities before a future broader attack.
The July ChatGPT three-file cancel case was a cancellation-after-commit or control/side-effect race.
The July ChatGPT case and Aug GitHub anomalies share a backend, cause or attacker.

G4_NETWORK_BRIDGE: require shared route/ASN/BGP/DNS/TLS/DPI/upstream evidence; temporal overlap alone fails
G5_GEOGRAPHIC_CONTROL: use witness geography only when self-reported/public; never infer it from handles
G6_TSPU_LONGITUDINAL_CONTROL: compare OONI and longitudinal measurements around Aug 26-28
G7_NEGATIVE_CONTROLS: preserve services/routes/repos/trigger paths that remained healthy

current_conclusion.strongest_new_external_fact: A selective TSPU-related DNS interference change was publicly observed beginning approximately the evening of Aug 26, contemporaneous with the wider investigation period.
current_conclusion.strongest_archaeology_fact: The Center-of-Storm traveler artifact is real, but its delayed/cancelled semantics are simulation-state semantics rather than network evidence.
current_conclusion.strongest_methodological_fact: JANUS already contains Temporal Continuity, Causal Isolation, CTC-cheat rejection and calibration rules requiring monotonic ordering, external freshness and frozen controls before promoting a timing anomaly.
unresolved: exact Riders of the Storm artifact
technical bridge from Russian TSPU changes to GitHub/OpenAI provider-side incidents
current_conclusion.final_claim_ceiling: The investigation may state that multiple real control-plane/network anomalies overlapped in time and that selective TSPU behavior is capable of fragmented effects. It may not state that Russia/TSPU caused GitHub or OpenAI outages, or that the observed TSPU changes were reconnaissance for a future attack, without additional evidence.
